build.recipe: Built LOCALLY on macOS, not on the Linux worker that produced v0622 and earlier. PATH shim exposing cargo-rch-real as `cargo`, then: RUSTFLAGS='--cap-lints=warn -C target-feature=+simd128' DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH=$TOOLCHAIN/lib wasm-pack build --release --target web --out-dir pkg_v0623 -- --features g1-learned
build.diagnostics: This build differs from v0622's in ways that are recorded here rather than glossed. (1) It was produced locally on macOS via wasm-pack, not by the Linux worker recipe, so no rawWasmSha256 pre-bindgen receipt is claimed and the byte-for-byte reproduction path of earlier versions does not apply. (2) It was built from a git worktree pinned to asupersync 05eb37c3 because that dependency's HEAD does not compile: supervision.rs calls ChildRegion::close_with_outcome and ::cancel_with_budget, which do not exist. (3) It is the first kernel built with the g1-learned feature and with simd128 enabled; that feature adds G1TransformerTrainerSession and is why the wasm exports changed. Despite the added trainer the artifact is 422 KB against 0.6.22's 441 KB. Dead-code diagnostics remain warnings, as before.

g1.armSwingGate: Clamped cubic smoothstep t*t*(3-2*t) in fixed physical seconds; changing gait frequency does not change the gate times. Shoulder and elbow swing is gated; posture and angular-velocity damping remain active.

browserResidualTrainer.optimizer: LM-CMA (fs-dfo) with IPOP restarts after 25 stalled generations
browserResidualTrainer.objective: the walking owner's own multi-factor objective, the same scalar CMA-ES minimises
browserResidualTrainer.baseline: zero policy head, which on a residual policy is exactly the tuned controller
browserResidualTrainer.playback: trace_packet(use_best) returns the standard packed G1 trace for the best policy or the tuned controller
browserResidualTrainer.resume: seed_head(head) re-scores a saved head and adopts it only if it beats the tuned controller
browserResidualTrainer.portableArithmetic: The transformer routes exp/tanh/sin/cos/powf through the libm crate rather than the host, so a policy trained natively scores the same here: baseline and distance agree to every digit and the objective to the 14th.
